title: Neurophysiology of Social Interaction: Influence of Peer Victimization and Social Anxiety
summary:
Many children and adolescents experience physical or emotional violence in their social environment, including peer victimization. Such negative experiences can significantly affect their well-being and increase the risk of mental health conditions such as social anxiety disorder.
This study examines how experiences of peer victimization affect the ability to interact socially, including in the context of social anxiety disorder. Using hyperscanning, the simultaneous measurement of brain activity of two interacting individuals, neurobiological mechanisms of social interactions will be analyzed. We will investigate how past experiences of abuse affect the ability to cooperate and process social feedback, and how this relates to social anxiety disorder.
The aim is to better understand the impact of peer violence and its relationship to social anxiety disorder. The results should help to develop new approaches for interventions to better support affected children and adolescents.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
IQ ≥ 85 
In the patient group: ICD-10 diagnosis of social anxiety disorder
Exclusion criteria:
IQ < 85
Presence of neuropsychiatric disorder
In healthy subjects: presence of a mental disorder according to ICD-10
